projection.title: Projection
projection.description: Present channels of existing devices as one new device of a chosen category.

transform.title: Numeric conversion
transform.description: Convert one reading into another, including calibration and NTC probes.

dewPoint.title: Dew point
dewPoint.description: Calculate the dew point from a temperature and a relative humidity sensor.

group.title: Actuator group

thermostat.title: Thermostat from relays

category.heading: Choose a category
category.description: Pick the kind of device you are creating. It determines which channels and properties the next step will ask you to map.

mapping.noRequired: This category has no required properties — map at least one to continue

shortcut.description: Take a whole channel: pick a channel on a real device and fill every property here that it can cover.
shortcut.applied: Filled {filled} of {total} properties from the selected channel.
shortcut.nothingApplied: The selected channel has no property this channel can use.

details.description: Give the device a name, and optionally assign it to a room and zones. A name is suggested from the category and room — you can change it.

review.noMappings: Nothing is mapped yet — go back and map at least one property.

hideSource.hint: Hides the source device from lists and pickers. It stays fully intact and can be unhidden again from the device list at any time.

selection.heading: Build a virtual device
selection.description: Made by splitting or combining channels and properties of devices that are already in Smart Panel.

layout.searchSources: Search by device, channel or room
layout.previewHint: Choose the sources to see a calculation preview.

measurement.name: Name
measurement.nativeCelsius: Native Celsius readings need no NTC conversion. NTC requires a voltage source and explicit probe parameters.
measurement.previewOnly: Preview only: this result is unqualified and never becomes a live reading.
measurement.measurementFinite: Enter every required finite numeric parameter.
measurement.measurementFailed: Measurement request failed. Retry after reloading.
measurement.measurementCatalog: Source catalog could not be loaded.

states.preview_revoked: Preview revoked; reload and preview again

measurement.filterCohort: Requires at least three qualified sources before filtering. Quorum counts retained sources, not weights.
measurement.aggregatePreviewOnly: Draft snapshot evaluated by the backend from currently qualified samples. It is read-only, expires with its evidence, and does not guarantee freshness or availability when saved. New sources may require fresh reports after creation.

help.legacyPrecision: Temperature keeps the precision defined by its output property.
help.precision: The result is rounded to steps of {step} {unit}.
help.quorum: This many inputs must remain valid and recent after exclusions. If fewer are available, the result is unavailable. For example, a minimum of 2 lets a group of 3 sensors keep working when one stops reporting.
help.filter: When enabled, readings farther from the middle value (median) than the maximum deviation are ignored. The deviation uses the selected unit. At least 3 valid, recent sensors are needed for comparison, and enough inputs must remain to meet the minimum.
help.maximumAge: Readings older than this many seconds are ignored. Choose a limit that leaves enough time for your sensors to send their next measurement.
help.previewDescription: This calculation uses readings available at the time shown below. Offline sensors or unavailable readings do not prevent saving the configuration. After creation, the device calculates values from new sensor reports.
help.reviewLoading: Checking the configuration and calculating the preview…

operators.mean: Adds the usable readings and divides by their count. Every sensor has the same influence.
operators.median: Uses the middle reading after sorting them. With an even number of readings, it averages the two middle values. This reduces the influence of extreme readings.
operators.weighted_mean: Calculates an average using the relative weight of each sensor. A sensor with weight 2 has twice the influence of one with weight 1.
operators.any: Reports detected when at least one usable input reports detection. No detection can be confirmed only when every configured input is usable and reports no detection.
operators.all: Reports detected only when every configured input is usable and reports detection. One usable input reporting no detection is enough to rule out detection.

help.processingAdvice: Start with the defaults. Set the maximum age a little longer than your sensors’ usual reporting interval. Lower the minimum if you want to allow calculations using fewer available sensors.

measurement.loadingCatalog: Loading settings and available measurement sources…

lightGroup.memberBounds: Select 2–256 distinct physical channels. Members remain individually controllable.
lightGroup.commonOnly: These optional controls are unavailable because every member must support a compatible contract.
lightGroup.loadFailed: The group could not be loaded.
lightGroup.revisionConflict: Configuration changed or a referenced control needs repair. Reload explicitly before trying again.
lightGroup.commandUncertain: The command result is uncertain. Refresh the reported state before issuing another command.
lightGroup.coverTypeGuide: Configure each physical cover TYPE as the same explicit singleton through its property metadata API: PATCH /api/v1/modules/devices/channels/<channel>/properties/<TYPE-property> with data.type and data.format, for example ["blind"]. Do not include data.value. Select the installed type yourself; names and models are not evidence.
lightGroup.coverCommandMeaning: OPEN/CLOSE confirms motion begun or an already reached endpoint, not full travel. STOP requires qualified stopped feedback.

wizard.detailsDescription: A group turns several actuators of the same kind into one device. Pick the kind first; it decides which devices you can add.
wizard.membersTitle: Which devices belong to the group?
wizard.membersDescription: A control is available only when every member supports it. The table shows each member and the controls the group will expose.
wizard.reviewTitle: Check the group before creating it
wizard.reviewDescription: Changing a control on the group changes it on every member. Members remain available as separate devices.
wizard.profileHelp: Required controls are always included. Additional controls follow from the devices you select.
wizard.controlsHint: Untick optional controls you do not want on the group.
wizard.controlsAdvice: Every member must support a compatible control, including its unit and range. Required controls cannot be turned off.
wizard.incompatibleMember: This device does not have compatible settings for the selected group.
wizard.coverHelp: All covers in a group must have the same configured type, such as blinds or shutters. The group only offers controls supported by every member.

comfort.title: Thermostat comfort
comfort.help: Comfort intent is separate from HVAC mode and physical activity. Safety guards always apply.
comfort.unconfigured: Comfort is not configured. Existing manual settings remain available.
comfort.offHeld: User OFF is latched. Presets and automation cannot resume output.
comfort.expiryHint: Countdown is informational. Server confirmation is required; it does not confirm output activity.
comfort.uncertain: Override state needs attention. Uncertain clocks inhibit output; unknown states require server confirmation.
comfort.offClearHelp: Clearing OFF is a separate explicit action and does not change the requested HVAC mode.
comfort.configHint: Enter only supported branch ranges and explicitly chosen preset temperatures in Celsius. No temperatures are supplied by default.
comfort.serverValidation: The server validates supported branches, ranges, deadband and revisions.

members.disconnection: I confirm the documented physical disconnection procedure
members.displayFloor: Display one member floor reading (protection unchanged)
members.mandatoryHelp: All members follow one room demand. One member fault inhibits the whole branch.
members.nativeUnavailable: Native-unit activation is unavailable until supported adapters are implemented.
members.recoveryHelp: Recovery retains ownership and forces OFF. It requires new qualification and real release proof.
members.removeLegacyGuard: Explicitly allow removal of the legacy global guard on save; affected members require restaging.
members.retained: Reservation retained. Use explicit recovery or release; ordinary removal cannot erase ownership.
members.sourceMismatch: Selected source is missing or no longer compatible. Retained identity is preserved.
members.qualificationHelp: Checks the installed guard and current target only. It does not establish controller readiness or certify physical equipment.
members.selectedFloorRequired: Select a compatible floor probe in Sensors for this safety extension.
members.noFailsafe: This output has no device-side failsafe. It can stay on if Smart Panel loses power or communication.
members.acknowledgeProtection: I have verified independent equipment protection for this output, including a floor limiter where required.
members.awaitingOff: Waiting for the device to report OFF. Its reservation is held and the opposite branch is blocked.
members.extensionUnavailable: The selected safety extension is unavailable for this output or configuration.
members.supervisedQualification: Software supervision requires independent protection and a fresh device report confirming OFF.

dewPoint.title: Dew point
dewPoint.boundary: Dew point is a distinct quantity. Both fresh inputs are required; it is not ambient or floor temperature.
dewPoint.installation: Cooling protection needs fresh dew-point and cooled-surface readings. A device-side extension may require a local probe.

errors.preview: Preview refused; check sources, policy and graph.
errors.revision: Configuration changed; reload and preview again.
errors.coolingPolicy: Enter an explicit positive cooling margin and recovery hysteresis of at most 60 °C.
errors.coolingMinimum: Enter a finite optional surface minimum above −45 °C and at most 60 °C.
errors.coolingDependencies: Each protected cooling output needs dew point, a cooled-surface probe and a valid maximum age.

dewPoint.description: Calculates the dew-point temperature from air temperature and relative humidity. It is a calculated measurement, not another air-temperature sensor.
dewPoint.sourcesDescription: Choose one air-temperature source and one relative-humidity source for the same environment. Adding another source replaces the one of that type. Offline sources can also be configured.
dewPoint.processingHelp: Maximum sample age sets how old each reading may be. Maximum timestamp skew limits the time difference between the temperature and humidity readings, so an old reading is not combined with a new one. Choose limits that match how often your sensors report.

diagnostics.skew: Source measurements are too far apart in time
diagnostics.graph_validation_pending: Source dependency graph is being checked

separateDevices.title: Temperature and humidity come from different devices
separateDevices.message: Separate sensors report at unrelated times, so their readings are rarely within the maximum timestamp skew ({skew} s) and the dew point is often unavailable. Choose both inputs from one combined temperature and humidity sensor.

nativeThermostat.title: Controller for an existing thermostat
nativeThermostat.delegation: The physical thermostat regulates temperature. No floor, condensation or opposed-output protection is provided.
nativeThermostat.name: Name
nativeThermostat.noCandidates: No eligible native thermostat is available.
nativeThermostat.acceptance: Acceptance is not physical confirmation. External changes are not automatically overridden.
nativeThermostat.singleOperation: One operation per request. Compound and automatic heat/cool requests are refused.
nativeThermostat.uncertain: Result uncertain. Refresh server state before another request.
nativeThermostat.drift: Observed settings differ from the request
nativeThermostat.releaseHelp: Release the Smart Panel reservation? This waits for issued work but sends no OFF command. The physical thermostat may continue regulating.

wizard.intro: This controller works with a real thermostat device. The device keeps regulating the temperature; Smart Panel sends it the requested mode and setpoints and shows what it reports back.
wizard.supported: Available devices and controls depend on the capabilities reported by the physical thermostat.
wizard.noCandidates: No suitable physical thermostat was found. Add your device to Smart Panel and check its configuration.

wizard.detailsDescription: Name the thermostat and choose its room and zones.
wizard.sourcesTitle: Which sensors should the thermostat use?
wizard.sourcesDescription: Choose room, floor or cooled-surface temperature for each reading. For cooling protection, also add a virtual Dew point reading. A window or door contact must be a boolean contact sensor.
wizard.actuatorsTitle: Which relays should control heating and cooling?
wizard.actuatorsDescription: Add relay outputs and choose whether each controls heating or cooling.
wizard.policyHelp: Setpoints are the target room temperatures. Tolerances reduce frequent switching around the target. Minimum OFF sets the pause before a relay can turn on again; changeover sets the pause between heating and cooling. Floor protection limits the floor temperature. Contact delays filter brief window openings, and temperature trend detection can pause regulation after a sudden temperature drop.
wizard.configurationTitle: How should the thermostat regulate temperature?
wizard.configurationDescription: Set temperatures, sample limits, delays and protection for the sensors and relays you selected.
wizard.sourceLimit: Choose each role once; up to eight cooled-surface sensors can be selected.
wizard.actuatorLimit: Up to eight relay outputs can be selected.
wizard.coolingSurfaceRequired: Select a compatible cooled-surface probe in Sensors.

draft.title: Draft controller
draft.description: The draft keeps the selected devices. Before enabling the thermostat, confirm independent protection for each software-supervised output and complete setup for any selected hardware extension.

thermostat.name: Thermostat name
thermostat.trend: Use ambient trend to infer open window without contact

sources.title: Temperature and contact sources
sources.help: Select sources that report the age of their original sample. Floor is an independent Celsius protection input; contact is optional.

conversion.rangesHelp: Input and output limits define where this conversion is valid. Enter both limits; values outside them are rejected, not forced to the nearest limit.
conversion.sampleHelp: The test input is optional. Enter a value inside the input range to see its calculated output. Leaving it blank checks the settings without a test calculation.
conversion.pointsHelp: Each calibration point pairs a measured input X with its known correct output Y. For example, 0 → 0 and 10 → 100 describe a scale. Add at least two points in increasing X order. The conversion follows straight lines between them and never extends beyond the first or last point.
conversion.thermistorHelp: Use the actual circuit and probe data: Vref is the divider supply voltage, Rfixed its fixed resistor, Rnom the probe resistance at Tnom, and beta or A/B/C come from the probe data sheet. Choose whether the probe is connected to ground or supply. These values are not guessed.
conversion.thermistorRequirement: NTC beta and Steinhart–Hart require a physical raw voltage source in V and a temperature output in °C. A sensor already reporting °C needs no thermistor conversion; use affine calibration if it needs an adjustment.

operators.affine: Affine applies output = scale × input + offset. Scale changes the size of a reading; offset adds a correction, such as subtracting a sensor bias.
operators.piecewise_linear: Piecewise linear conversion uses known calibration pairs and calculates values between neighbouring points.
operators.ntc_beta: NTC beta converts raw divider voltage to Celsius using the probe’s nominal resistance, nominal temperature and beta coefficient.
operators.steinhart_hart: Steinhart–Hart converts raw divider voltage to Celsius using the probe’s A, B and C coefficients.
operators.extension: An extension supplies the conversion. Select its definition and enter the required parameters within their shown bounds.

validation.positiveNumber: Enter a number greater than zero.
validation.rangeOrder: The minimum must not exceed the maximum.
validation.pointOrder: Enter numeric X/Y pairs with unique X values in increasing order.
validation.pointCoverage: Calibration points must cover the entire input range.
validation.coefficientsNonzero: At least one coefficient must be nonzero.
validation.parameterBounds: Fill in required parameters within their declared bounds.
validation.operatorRanges: Stay inside the ranges declared by the operator.
validation.ageBounds: Enter a whole number of seconds from 1 to 86400.
validation.sampleOptional: No test value: only the configuration will be checked.
validation.sampleBounds: Use a test value inside the input range; thermistor voltage must also be between zero and Vref.
validation.notChecked: Fix the highlighted settings, then check again.

sourceReporting.observed: This sensor reports about every {typical} (longest gap {longest}).
sourceReporting.observedSlowest: The slowest of these sensors reports about every {typical} (longest gap {longest}).

unknown.title: Reporting interval not known yet
unknown.message: Smart Panel has not seen enough reports from this sensor since it started. Battery radio sensors (Zigbee, Bluetooth) often report only every 30–60 minutes: set the maximum age a little longer than that, or come back later for a recommendation.
unknown.messageMany: Smart Panel has not seen enough reports from some of these sensors since it started. Battery radio sensors (Zigbee, Bluetooth) often report only every 30–60 minutes: set the maximum age a little longer than that, or come back later for a recommendation.

tooShort.title: The maximum age is shorter than this sensor’s reporting interval
tooShort.titleMany: The maximum age is shorter than the reporting interval of one of these sensors
tooShort.message: Between reports the reading goes stale. {consequence} A longer age keeps it usable, with a reading that can be up to that old.

consequence.ambient: The thermostat stops heating and cooling until the next report arrives.
consequence.contact: The window state counts as unknown, and the thermostat pauses until the next report arrives.
consequence.floor: Heating is blocked until the next report arrives.
consequence.surface: Cooling is blocked until the next report arrives.
consequence.aggregate: The sensor is left out of the result, and the value becomes unavailable when fewer valid sources remain than the minimum.
consequence.converter: The converted value is unavailable until the next report arrives.
consequence.dewPoint: The dew point is unavailable until the next report arrives.

windowDetection.requirement: Window detection needs a room temperature reading at least every {required}.
windowDetection.fits: The room sensor reports about every {typical}.

tooSlow.title: The room sensor reports too rarely for window detection
tooSlow.message: It reports about every {typical}, and detection needs a reading at least every {required}. Sensors that report on change speed up while the temperature falls, but rarely that much. Without enough readings detection never pauses the thermostat; it only misses open windows. For reliable detection, add a window contact.
